title: Mathesis computation certificate
description: SPEC-STREAM0 §6.4. A certificate is a claim that a dumb exact checker can REPLAY. That is the whole definition of 'solver' in this programme: not a thing that computes an answer, but a thing that emits a record another program can independently re-decide. A certificate that cannot be replayed by a checker simpler than the producer is not a certificate.

claim.description: The statement being certified, self-contained and falsifiable. No adjectives. A reader must be able to tell what would refute it without running anything.

engine.description: A = exact algebra (rational identity/inequality harness). B = enclosures (rounded-rational interval trajectories; claim form 'for all t in [0,T], state is in boxes'). C = PIVP / poly-algebraic compilation, which composes: its integration stage is an Engine B run.

inputs_sha256.description: Digest of the exact inputs. Determinism is a hard requirement (HARDNESS.md H9): the same digest must yield the same verdict on any machine, or the certificate certifies nothing.

replay_cmd.description: One command that re-decides the claim from the recorded inputs. Must exit 0 for PASS and non-zero for FAIL -- a replayer that only ever reports success is the checker-that-cannot-fail (HARDNESS.md H2).

negative_controls.description: Controls demonstrated to FAIL. At least one is required. The control that counts is the plausible near-miss -- a tampered certificate, a perturbed identity, an honest-failure case (e.g. inviscid blow-up for Engine B) -- not obvious garbage.

tier.description: B for a replayed exact-arithmetic claim. B-dyn for an enclosure certificate. NOTE: whether B-dyn may ever gate a tier promotion is an OPEN question reserved to the human owner (SPEC-STREAM0 §11); until it is settled, B-dyn is recorded and not relied upon. B-dyn's position in the tier order is likewise unsettled -- see docs/designs/RECONCILIATION.md §2.1.

meta.description: Reproduction context. Absent versions make a failed replay undiagnosable a year later, which is when replays are actually attempted.

ledger_id.description: The claim id this certificate justifies. A certificate with no ledger row supports nothing that may be cited (SPEC.md §0).
